title: Capacity rundown and oddities — weekly log
summary: Weekly engineering rundown focused on regional GPU capacity signals, two small oddities in priming behavior this week, and near-term mitigations to avoid customer-impacting latency spikes.
content:
Context:
We ran a capacity pass for the week of 2029-03-11 focused on three regions (us-west1, eu-north1, ap-southeast1) to validate priming heuristics and the new opportunistic backfill rules. This note collects the operational signals, a couple of low-likelihood oddities we observed, immediate mitigations, and proposed follow-ups for the next two sprints.

Headline metrics (rolling 24h snapshots):
- cluster-wide GPU utilization (avg): 72%
- prewarm hit rate (requests served from warm pool): 68% (target 75%)
- average tail priming latency (p95 extra time to first token when cold): 420ms (target < 300ms)
- failed allocation rate (ephemeral jobs): 0.9% (baseline 0.3%)
- cross-region overflow reroutes: 14 in 24h (mostly eu->us bursts)

This week highlights:
1) us-west1 burst window at 03/12 08:20–08:40 PST produced a series of short-lived ephemeral allocations that caused local prioritization to throttle Dedicated pools for ~7 minutes. No customer SLA violations recorded, but p95 latency for small text-gen routes spiked to ~1.2s.
2) We deployed the opportunistic-backfill tuning (GH:fleet-allocator#279) to increase fill-rate for idle preemptible nodes; observed improved amortized unit cost but saw a temporary rise in failed allocation rate (see metrics above).
3) ap-southeast1 showed a downward trend in prewarm hit rate after a config drift incident on 03/11 where a rollout reverted cache TTLs to 30s from 300s (rolled back by infra-config-ops).

Oddities observed (these are unusual and need hypotheses):
A) Periodic priming latency oscillation in eu-north1: every ~90 minutes during the 24h window priming delay p95 jumped ~250ms for ~3–5 minutes, then recovered. No corresponding CPU/GPU saturation.
- Hypothesis A1: KV cache eviction race when multiple model variants are being hot-swapped by rollout automation.
- Hypothesis A2: Storage-layer small-I/O latency tail (artifact store) causing cache miss amplification.
- Quick check done: correlated artifact-store p99 I/O with spikes — weak correlation (r~0.2). Next step: enable higher-resolution KV cache ops logging for one host pool during next burst window.

B) Low-volume allocation failures clustered to a small subset of hosts in us-west1 (hostnames start with preempt-uw-9*). Failures are consistent with ephemeral node boot-time timeouts during kernel module initialization.
- Hypothesis B1: driver/kernel module mismatch after the 03/09 kernel roll (some nodes still on old bootstrap image).
- Mitigation taken: cordoned the affected host group and queued a rolling reprovision morning patch (INFRA-4321).

Immediate mitigations (already enacted):
- Raised prioritization weight for Dedicated pools in us-west1 during the burst window; emergency rule reverted post-burst.
- Reverted cache TTL drift in ap-southeast1 and forced a cache warm pass for top-20 routes.
- Cordoned preempt-uw-9* hosts; scheduled reprovisioning for 03/15 AM.

Near-term items (next 2 sprints):
- Observatory task: instrument KV cache eviction traces and add a short-lived sampler to capture pre/post-eviction request latencies (owner: Liam, JIRA INFRA-4387).
- Capacity plan update: add a 10% soft-buffer to Dedicated headroom in us-west1 for predicted marketing-driven bursts (owner: Sofia).
- Failover policy tweak: test expanded cross-region reroute policy for eu->us overflow to prefer us-central1 (lower latency than current us-west) during eu surge windows.
- Reliability experiment: run a small canary of improved boot-time image with upgraded kernel modules on a 2-host pool to validate reprovision before wide rollout (owner: Daniel).

Questions/asks for SRE on-call this week:
- Can we get a timeline for reprovisioning the preempt-uw-9* fleet? (Daniel has the handoff ticket).
- Will the storage team surface any scheduled maintenance windows that could explain the eu-north1 periodic bursts?

Risk assessment:
- Customer impact: low immediate risk (no SLA breaches) but medium latent risk if priming oscillation correlates with high request rates.
- Complexity: medium; cross-team (storage, release-engineering, fleet-allocator) coordination required.

Action items (owners and expected dates):
- INFRA-4321: reprovision preempt-uw-9* hosts (owner: Daniel Okoye) — ETA 2029-03-15
- INFRA-4387: KV eviction tracing rollout on one eu-north1 pool (owner: Liam Chen) — ETA 2029-03-18
- Capacity-Roll: add 10% Dedicated headroom for us-west1 (owner: Sofia Martinez) — ETA 2029-03-20
- Fleet-allocator PR follow-up: validate backfill tuning metrics and revert knob if failed allocation > 1.5% for 12h (owner: Maya Rivera) — ongoing

Notes / running hypotheses log (freeform):
- The eu-north1 oscillation is the most nagging; it behaves like a short-duration coordinated event rather than isolated host flakiness. Could be a background refresh job (we have a remediation agent that refreshes model-kv every 90m by default). Check alignment.
- Prewarm hit rate dip in ap-southeast1 was operator error on the rollout config (reminder: add a preflight assert to infra-config-ops pipeline).

Meeting cadence & next check-in:
- We'll review the tracing sample from eu-north1 in Monday ops sync (2029-03-18).
- Short triage huddle mid-week if reprovision shows rollout issues (standup invite pending).
